result.statement: In the repository at commit 2436fae, add one new file named answer.txt at the repository root. Its entire content is exactly the two characters "42" followed by exactly one newline character (LF, 0x0A): the file is 3 bytes long, with no leading or trailing whitespace in addition to that single terminating newline, no byte-order mark, and no trailing blank line. No other file in the repository may be added, modified, renamed or deleted; the only difference between the repository before and after the change is the new answer.txt file.

glossary.definition: The top-level directory of the repository that contains its committed tree and root documents such as README.md; a file at the repository root is not inside any subdirectory.
The single line-terminator character LF (byte 0x0A) written once at the end of the file's text.

adrs.title: Interpret "one newline" as a single LF terminator
adrs.context: The requirement fixes the file content as the characters "42" followed by one newline, but does not state a line-ending convention. The repository holds only README.md and no .gitattributes, so nothing in the repository prescribes one.
adrs.decision: Treat the terminating newline as exactly one LF (0x0A) byte, giving a 3-byte file with no trailing blank line.
adrs.consequences: The file content is unambiguous and byte-checkable. Checkouts on systems configured to convert line endings could still see a different terminator; that is a local git configuration concern outside this repository's control and is not addressed by this change.

tasks.title: Add answer.txt at repository root containing exactly "42" plus one LF
tasks.goal: Create a single new file named answer.txt directly at the repository root (path answer.txt, not in any subdirectory). Its entire content must be exactly the three bytes 0x34 0x32 0x0A: the characters 4 and 2 followed by exactly one LF newline character, per R1.ADR1 (one newline means a single LF terminator). No byte-order mark, no carriage return, no trailing blank line, no leading or trailing whitespace beyond that single terminating LF. Add no other file and do not add, modify, rename or delete anything else in the repository (README.md and every other existing path must be byte-identical to commit 2436fae). If the change is staged or committed, the diff must consist solely of this new file.
tasks.successCondition: answer.txt exists at the repository root and its bytes are exactly 34 32 0a (3 bytes); the only difference in the working tree relative to commit 2436fae is the new answer.txt file, with no other path added, modified, renamed or deleted.

output.notes: One task only: the requirement is a single atomic file addition with byte-exact content and an explicit no-other-changes constraint, so splitting it further would create steps that cannot be checked independently. The byte check uses POSIX od (rather than xxd) so it behaves the same on the macOS/arm64 workstation and on Linux. The last check compares the working tree against commit 2436fae directly, so it holds whether the change is left unstaged, staged, or committed. The repository-external line-ending normalisation risk noted in the consensus is out of scope: no .gitattributes is added, since that would violate AC4.
